Desist

/dih-ZIST/ — rhymes with "resist" · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To desist is to stop doing something, especially something you have been asked or told to stop.

The judge ordered the company to desist from using the stolen logo.

Worked Example

After the copyright notice arrived, the website designer agreed to desist from copying images from that artist's portfolio, knowing she had been formally warned.

Desist carries a formal, commanding tone and often implies that someone in authority has demanded the stop. Just saying "stopped" wouldn't capture the sense of compliance with a directive or legal demand.

How Desist Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

refrain

refrain: to hold yourself back from acting

cease

cease: to bring an activity to an end

abstain

abstain: to deliberately avoid doing something entirely

Antonyms

persist

persist: to keep going despite being told

continue

continue: to carry on without any stop

How Strong Is It? — pause → stop → desist → abstain

pause vs. desist

pause vs. desist: Pause is much weaker than desist — pausing only breaks off an action for a moment, while to desist is to stop it altogether, usually after being told to.

stop vs. desist

stop vs. desist: Stop is weaker than desist; stop is the plain, everyday word for ending an action, while desist adds a formal, final sense of quitting for good, often on command.

abstain vs. desist

abstain vs. desist: Abstain is stronger than desist — desisting means stopping something you were doing, while abstaining means deliberately holding yourself back from it entirely, often as a lasting commitment.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: away from, off (Latin)

Root — sist

Root — sist: to stand; come to a stop (from sistere) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: De- ('away from') plus sist ('to stand, come to a stop') gives 'to stand away from' an activity — to desist is to bring yourself to a stop and step away from what you were doing.

Use the root in a new word: persist

Use the root in a new word: persist: Someone who persists keeps standing firm and refuses to quit — the exact opposite of someone who desists, who stops and stands away from what they were doing.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal

Desist sounds formal and legal — the word used in official warnings and court orders. For everyday stopping, "stop" is the natural choice. Use desist when the stopping responds to authority or follows a serious directive.
